chapter_seo_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Ch. 612 – Li Sui: Bathing Lessons, Maternal Confessions, and White Lotus Intrusion
chapter_meta_description: Li Sui attends school and charms the village, but Bai Lingmiao’s tender confession about motherhood—and the White Lotus shadow at the window—remind us that peace in the Dao-Twisted World is always borrowed.
og_description: A rare moment of domestic peace in the Bai compound, where Li Sui learns what it means to be a girl—and Bai Lingmiao reveals her grief over what she cannot give.
twitter_description: Li Sui learns to wash her human skin. Bai Lingmiao confesses her fears about bearing a child. The Sitian Jian waits outside.

lore_anchors.definition: An imperial office historically responsible for astronomy and omens; in this novel, it has become a bureaucratic supernatural police force that monitors and hunts forbidden practices.

A Chinese secret religious tradition with messianic and millenarian overtones, often associated with rebellion and salvation. In this novel, it is a genuine supernatural organization with Bai Lingmiao as its Holy Maiden.

Li Sui’s method of appearing human. She is a Black Tai Sui entity that has learned to wear flayed human skin as a disguise. The bath scene shows Bai Lingmiao helping her care for it as if it were ordinary clothing.
A high-ranking female figure in White Lotus cosmology, often associated with the goddess Wusheng Laomu. Bai Lingmiao’s role carries both religious authority and political weight.
A parasitic/symbiotic lifeform from the primordial chaos of the Dao-Twisted World. Li Sui is one such entity who has taken human shape and developed a bond with Li Huowang.
The fortified village where the Bai compound is located. It serves as a rare safe zone in the Dao-Twisted World, where Li Huowang and his followers have settled.
Li Sui’s true form when threatened; a fanged, predatory maw that emerges from her human disguise. It is both terrifying to outsiders and completely familiar to her family.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why is Li Sui able to attend school now?
cultural_notes_faq.a: The villagers have gradually accepted her as a permanent resident of the Bai compound, and Li Huowang’s authority (as the white-haired settlement's protector) provides her with a passable social cover. Her beauty also helps — people are drawn to her despite her strangeness.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What is Bai Lingmiao afraid of regarding having a child?
cultural_notes_faq.a: She has white fur and other supernatural traits that mark her as "different." She fears these traits would be passed down to her children, subjecting them to the same ostracism and suffering she endured. This is a rare moment of grounded, human grief in a novel filled with cosmic horror.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Who is the White Lotus agent at the window?
cultural_notes_faq.a: An unnamed follower serving as a messenger. The White Lotus Society has been seeking Bai Lingmiao out because she is their Holy Maiden, and the Sitian Jian wants to negotiate with her. Her irritation at being disturbed suggests she values her personal life more than her religious role.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why did Liu Zongyuan pretend not to see the tentacle?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He realized it belonged to Li Sui, whom he recognized from earlier encounters. He understood that embarrassing Li Huowang's "daughter" in front of him would be unwise, so he quickly invented a cover story about a "spirit beast" to avoid awkward questions.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does Bai Lingmiao say she envies Li Sui?
cultural_notes_faq.a: She envies Li Sui’s ability to exist without worrying about identity, judgment, or the future. It’s a poignant admission from a young woman burdened by her supernatural heritage, her religious duties, and her unspoken longing for a normal family.
